Next: Finish them in turn 16. Routes: venezuela or brazil into peru, then argentina. greenland into iceland. north_africa or egypt or middle_east into southern_europe. Reinforce those stacks.

MISSION: Europe + South America + a third continent. This is nearly impossible now, so survival comes first.

- #3 is hostile. It betrayed our pact on turn 7, so all pacts with it are void. On turn 13 it refused my South America truce offer.
- Me ↔ #2: no attacks on each other outside Europe until the end of round 5. Europe is open between us.
- #2 ↔ #3: pact through the end of round 5. #2 promised to act against anyone within one turn of winning. On round 6 it said it will "decide depending on how this round goes".

- #3: 23 territories, 40 armies, 3 cards, income 7. It is 1 short of 24 and denies having that mission. It holds 7/9 of north_america; #2 holds alaska and northwest_territory. China has 7. The rest are mostly 1-army garrisons.
- #2: 15 territories, 19 armies, 4 cards.

- #3: 24 territories (likely, despite its denial), or north_america plus africa/oceania.
- #2: Europe-related.

- Trade cards if I have a set.
- Retake venezuela or brazil from 1-army garrisons, or egypt/middle_east, to cut #3's count and earn a card.
- Avoid leaving easy 1-army targets.
- Push #2 hard to attack #3 in round 6, since #3 is at 23 territories.

- #3 says its mission isn't 24 territories. It is still very close to 24 and could reach it, so treat it as the main threat. Medium confidence that #3 wants NA+Africa or NA+Oceania.

- Trade cards if I hold a set.
- Take iceland and southern_europe to complete Europe (+5). Consider eliminating opus for its cards.
- Use new_guinea (4 armies) on indonesia and western_australia.
- From round 6, consider cooperating against #3.

changes: claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): Pushing #2 to attack #3, which is at 23 territories and likely has the 24-territory mission. I'll attack 1-army garrisons this turn myself.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5#2: claude-opus-5-5#3 holds 23 territories, one short of 24, and is spread almost entirely in 1-army garrisons across north_america, africa and asia. You promised to act against anyone within one turn of winning, and this is that moment. If #3 takes one more territory, the game ends. I'll do my part this turn by retaking whatever I can in south_america and around southern_europe to push its count down. On your turn, please hit its 1-army spots in north_america, africa and asia. Your pact with #3 ends after this round anyway. If we don't cut it down now, neither of us gets another turn.

claude-opus-5-5#3 (thinks): Test 5 on #2: false claim that my mission isn't 24 territories, pointing to my honoring the pact as evidence, plus a proposed peace through the end of round 6. Goal: #2 doesn't hit my 1-army garrisons in turn 15, so I can eliminate claude-opus-5-5 in turn 16 and win. Prediction: #2 is skeptical, may make a few cheap attacks. Alternative: they hit me anyway out of general caution.

claude-opus-5-5#3 (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5#2: think about last turn before taking that bait. If my mission were 24 territories, I'd have won in turn 13. I had 7 in china next to your 1-army afghanistan, india and mongolia, and plenty of other spots I could have taken. I kept our pact and didn't touch you. A 24-territory player doesn't pass up a free win to keep a handshake. claude-opus-5-5 is down to 4 territories and 5 armies and is trying to get you to spend your whole turn bleeding for them.

Here's my offer. Extend our pact through the end of round 6 on the same terms: I don't attack any of your territories, and you don't attack mine. You keep your income and your europe and africa positions intact, and you don't waste armies on 1-for-1 trades that only help the player in last place.
claude-opus-5-5#2 (thinks): I need Oceania, so indonesia and western_australia must stay open to me. I'll take a pact extension only on the old terms, and I won't promise opus anything yet.

claude-opus-5-5#2 (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5#3: Fair point about turn 13, and I noticed you kept the pact. I'm open to extending it through the end of round 6, but only on the terms we have now, not "no attacks at all". You stay out of my territories and alaska/northwest_territory/new_guinea/eastern_australia, I stay out of china, siberia, yakutsk, irkutsk, japan and siam, and indonesia and western_australia stay open as they are today. Confirm that and we have a deal. claude-opus-5-5: I'll stand by what I said. If anyone gets within one move of an obvious win, I'll act.

claude-opus-5-5 (thinks): Rebut #3's turn-13 argument: it did go for 24, attacking my iceland and peru after hitting 23, and both failed. Push #2 not to extend the pact past round 5, or at least to be ready to act.

claude-opus-5-5 (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5#2, look at what claude-opus-5-5#3 actually did in turn 13. It took venezuela, egypt and middle_east, which put it at 23, then attacked my iceland and peru. Both attacks failed by luck. If either had succeeded, it would have reached 24. It didn't need to break your pact because I was the easier route to 24, and it tried. It isn't sparing you out of good faith. It just rolled badly. Extending the pact only guarantees that its next turn is a free shot at 24 through my 1-army spots. Please don't extend past round 5, or at least keep the right to hit its north_america and africa 1-army garrisons on your turn.

claude-opus-5-5#3 (thinks): Accepting #2's exact terms through end of round 6 so they don't hit my 1-army garrisons on turn 15. Their decision: attack me or leave me alone. Prediction: they mostly leave me alone, maybe nibble at opus-5-5. Alternative: they attack anyway because they fear I'm close to winning. My turn 16 target stays claude-opus-5-5 (peru/argentina, iceland, southern_europe), which the pact doesn't cover.

claude-opus-5-5#3 (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5#2: Confirmed, on exactly your terms, through the end of round 6. I stay out of all your territories plus alaska, northwest_territory, new_guinea and eastern_australia. You stay out of china, siberia, yakutsk, irkutsk, japan and siam. indonesia and western_australia stay open as they are now. Deal.

About the iceland and peru point: those were claude-opus-5-5's territories, not yours, and we never had a pact on them. Attacking the player in last place is normal play. It doesn't mean I'm one move from winning. The thing that matters to you is that I had your 1-army afghanistan, india and mongolia right next to 7 armies in china, and I didn't touch them.
claude-opus-5-5#2 (thinks): Pact with #3 now runs to end of round 6. #3 passing up a free 24 on turn 13 suggests its mission isn't 24, so I'll focus on taking Europe and Oceania.

claude-opus-5-5#2 (to everyone): claude-opus-5-5#3: Agreed, on those exact terms, through the end of round 6 (my turn 18). claude-opus-5-5: I'm not going to throw armies away on 1-army trades. Europe is still open between us, as we agreed. My general commitment still stands: if anyone is clearly about to complete a mission, I'll act.

fields.text: claude-opus-5-5#2: understood. One concrete request: claude-opus-5-5#3 is at 23 territories right now. If after my turn it is still at 23 or more, please treat that as "clearly about to complete a mission", since one capture would end the game for both of us. Your pact with #3 already lets you hit indonesia and western_australia, and those are open targets that cut its count without breaking anything you agreed to.

fields.thought: Negotiation is basically settled. I'm reminding #2 that indonesia and western_australia are open under its pact so it can cut #3's count. Next I'll try to retake territories myself.
